questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The courses that I would attend were crucial. Furthermore active fieldwork was essentiel.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: An overall very good expirence both academically and personally.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Semi easy. The online system was at times very complicated but manageable.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Overall satisfied but more social events would have been nice to get to know my fellow students better at the beginning.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Theres is only on place for students to live in town. An apartment here is guaranteed upon arrival.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Very easy, no problem at all.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: perfect!

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very complicated and confusing.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: On the UNIS website you can see how to apply, so I followed their guide. But following their guide takes you to UiT's application portal, which I wasn't aware of. I was an exchange student through UiT to UNIS, so I didn't give it much thought. But when I didn't get an answer from UNIS long after the deadline, I contacted them and was told that I had applied incorrectly and therefore had not been offered a place anyway and they had forgotten to inform me about it. Therefore, I could only get a place if another student declined their place. Luckily, someone did and I got a place. All in all, it was a very confusing and stressful process.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Contact via e-mail or phone

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I originally wanted to take some other courses, but I was not approved for them and therefore ended up with the only courses I was approved for and therefore had no real choice in terms of my courses.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Double check everything! Rather call the institution the be sure of everything.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very good! A bit stressfull at times with every papers and project at once.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Very appropriate. Same level if not a bit higher than at home. A lot of fieldwork which was very nice!

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: fewer people and no lectures only classroom teaching. A lot more fieldwork than at home.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: AG-210 and AG-211

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: AG-210 and AG-211 both very good and interesting courses with a lot of learning by doing.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: lots of opportunities, but nothing party related really and not much to socialize with other studies than my own.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: gym, swimming pool, kayak, sauna, cinema, knitting nights, game nights, waffle nights, student led lectures, hiking clubs

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: knitting nights, game nights and waffle nights were very cozy and a nice way to get to know people.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go dog sledding, go sailing, go hiking, museum visit.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: not difficult at all.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: participate in school and student-run activities

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: none.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Similar to my own.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
socialise with other students
enjoy nature, mountains, wildlife and the sea
enjoy the culture and history

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not really.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: New friendships and memoris

questions.answer: The dark period. No sun for the last month was very challenging
